newsitem.title: USA: U.S. adj retail sales up 0.2 pct in April -- Redbook.
newsitem.headline: U.S. adj retail sales up 0.2 pct in April -- Redbook.

text.p: U.S. seasonally adjusted retail sales rose 0.2 percent for the first three weeks of fiscal April versus March, according to the Lynch, Jones & Ryan Inc Redbook Retail Sales Index.
The index rose 6.1 percent compared to the same month a year ago, the report said. Adjusted retail sales rose 5.6 percent in the week ended April 26 compared with the same week a year ago, it said.

"It looks as if April is not going to turn out to be a good month, even though next week should be better," said Howard Eilenberg, retail analyst at Lynch, Jones & Ryan, in an interview with Reuters Financial Television.
Sales in the past week centered around gardening goods, pharmaceutical items and higher-priced apparel, he said.
Continued slow sales growth may lead to more discounting, the analyst said. "As the season progresses, if they're not selling all their goods, they're going to have to mark them down," he said.
Eilenberg said a decline in the Redbook index could be a leading indicator of an economic slowdown, but added it was too early to draw any conclusions about the direction of consumer demand.
